lesson.subject: numeracy
lesson.title: Percentage of an Amount
lesson.subtitle: Term 4 Week 6, Session 5
lesson.footer: Fractions, Decimals and Percentages | Year 5/6 Maths | Session 5

plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Number, Year 5 (VC2M5N06, VC2M5N07): finding percentages of amounts with efficient mental and written multiplication and division, checking reasonableness
plan.shape: short-cycle loops: benchmark percentages (50%, 25%, 10%), then building from 10% and 1%, because each builds on the one before
plan.criticalFeature: find a benchmark you know (50%, 25%, 10%, 1%), then build the percentage from it
plan.anchor: one amount, three names: fraction, decimal, percentage; make it out of 100 to switch
plan.catchUp: Missed earlier sessions? Show 25% = 1/4 and 10% = 1/10 on a hundred grid before the launch.

studentTools: Printed Worksheet for every student; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: The week's anchor on the board: one amount, three names: fraction, decimal, percentage; make it out of 100 to switch
Benchmarks: 50% = halve, 25% = halve again, 10% = divide by 10, 1% = divide by 100

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn. Benchmark percentages, a percentage table, building from 10%, a mistake, and sport and shopping problems.
resources.title: Percentage of an Amount
resources.subtitle: Find a benchmark, then build.

items.prompt: Find each percentage of the amount.
Liv found 20% of 35. Find her mistake and fix it.

example.prompt: A $60 footy jumper is 25% off. How much do you save?

items.prompt: A stadium holds 48 000 people. It is 75% full. How many people are there?
A $120 pair of runners is 30% off. What is the sale price?

items.explain: 10% of 900 = 90 and 90% of 100 = 90. They are equal.

items.prompt: Make up a sale-price problem with an answer of $30 saved. Show it works.
items.answer: For example: a $120 item with 25% off saves $30, or a $300 item with 10% off.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option. Working back to the whole, comparing two discounts, and a percentage increase, with worked examples.
resources.title: Extension: Percentage Challenges
resources.subtitle: Work backwards. Compare deals.

example.prompt: 10% of a number is 7. What is the number?

items.prompt: 25% of a number is 18. What is the number?
30% of a crowd is 600 people. How big is the whole crowd?
5% of a prize is $40. What is the whole prize?

example.prompt: $50 shoes: 20% off, or $8 off. Which is better?

items.prompt: For each item, which deal saves more?

example.prompt: A $40 ticket goes up by 10%. New price?

items.prompt: A club had 250 members. Membership grew by 20%. How many members now?

resources.label: Supported Worksheet
resources.description: For students who need more guidance: benchmarks only, a step frame and a hint on every question.
resources.title: Percentages of Amounts: Step by Step
resources.subtitle: Halve for 50%. Halve again for 25%. Divide by 10 for 10%.

slides.notes: Session 5 of our fractions, decimals and percentages week: today we find a percentage of an amount.
Before you start, put boards and markers on every desk, and write the benchmarks on the board. Print the Worksheet for everyone, and a few copies of the Extension and the Supported Worksheet.

slides.title: Translate a point
prompts: (-1, 3) moves 4 right and 5 down. Where does it land?

beats: SAY: Let's warm up with coordinates and area.
ASK: Where does negative 1, 3 land after 4 right and 5 down?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: (3, -2)
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> one move at a time on the four-quadrant grid. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Negative 1 add 4 is 3,
and 3 take away 5 is negative 2. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing (-5, 8).
Fix: ask which way right and down go, and they redo it.
notes.prep: Review of Week 2 coordinates (the request named the focus). Keep the review under 6 minutes.

beats: ASK: Which quadrant is negative 2, negative 5 in?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: the third
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> say left or right, then up or down. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Left and down: the third quadrant. Tick it or fix it.
trap: saying the fourth.
Fix: ask whether negative 2 is left or right, and they rename it.

slides.title: Perimeter and area
prompts: A rectangle is 15 m by 6 m. Find its perimeter and its area.

beats: ASK: What are the perimeter and the area
of a 15 metre by 6 metre rectangle?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 42 m and 90 m²
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then on to Fluency.
Less -> trace the edge for perimeter, shade the inside for area. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Perimeter: 15 and 6 is 21, doubled is 42 metres.
Area: 15 times 6 is 90 square metres. Tick it or fix it.
trap: swapping perimeter and area.
Fix: say perimeter goes around, area covers, and they check.

beats: SAY: Now for our eight times table.
Write each answer as fast as you can.
ASK: What is 8 times 5?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 40
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> 8 tens is 80, halve it. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 40. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 35 or 45.
Fix: half of 8 tens is 40, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Times tables fluency. Keep the whole block under 5 minutes.

beats: SAY: Here's a bigger one.
ASK: What is 8 times 25?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 200
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> 4 twenty-fives is 100, double it. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 200. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 180.
Fix: 4 twenty-fives is 100, so 8 is 200, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

beats: SAY: Now a division. How many eights make 88?
ASK: What is 88 divided by 8?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 11
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the learning intention.
Less -> 10 eights is 80, then one more 8. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 11. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 10 or 12.
Fix: 10 eights is 80, one more is 88, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to find a percentage of an amount using benchmarks and multiplication.
successCriteria: I can find 50%, 25% and 10% of an amount.
I can build any percentage from 10% and 5% or 1%.
I can check my answer makes sense and explain how.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: This week we learned three names for one amount.
Today we use percentages to find part of an amount.
SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we start,
and the second one is our big goal today.
notes.prep: SC1 benchmarks are reachable for everyone; SC2 building from 10% is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 checking reasonableness is the stretch.

slides.title: Half price!
slides.prompt: A $64 game is 50% off. How much do you save?

beats: POINT to the price.
SAY: Some of you may have seen a 50 percent off sale.
Here's a game for 64 dollars.
ASK: If the game is 50 percent off, how much do you save?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $32
SCAN boards for 32.
80%+ -> cold call one student: How did you work it out so fast?
Less -> say 50 percent is a half, and halve 64 together. Re-ask.
SAY: 50 percent is a half, so you save 32 dollars.
Today we find other percentages using benchmarks like that.
trap: writing $14, by subtracting 50.
Fix: say 50 percent is a half, and they halve.
notes.prep: The launch comes after the LI: 50% as a half. Under 4 minutes.

slides.meaning: An easy, known amount you use to work out harder ones.

beats: POINT to the word.
SAY: This word is benchmark. Say it with me: bench-mark.
SAY: A benchmark is an easy amount we know,
that helps us work out harder ones.
Fifty, twenty-five, ten and one percent are our benchmarks.
ASK: What is 10 percent of 70?
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 7
trap: writing 60.
Fix: say 10 percent is a tenth, and they divide.
notes.prep: Benchmarks are the anchor for today.

beats: POINT to the bar.
SAY: Here's 120 split into four quarters. Each quarter is 25 percent, and that's 30.
MODEL each benchmark.
SAY: 50 percent, I halve: 60. 25 percent, I halve again: 30.
10 percent, I divide by 10: 12.
ASK: For 360, what are 50 percent, 25 percent and 10 percent?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Halve 360: 180. Halve again: 90. Divide by 10: 36.
trap: finding 25% by dividing by 25.
Fix: say 25 percent is a quarter, and they halve twice.
notes.help: Draw the bar and split it into quarters or tenths.
notes.prep: The benchmarks everything else builds from. SC1.

beats: MODEL finding 10% of 80.
SAY: To find 35 percent of 80, I start with my benchmark.
10 percent of 80 is 8.
MODEL building 35%.
SAY: 30 percent is three lots of 8, which is 24.
5 percent is half of 10 percent: 4. So 35 percent is 28.
ASK: Use the same steps. What is 15 percent of 60?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 9
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 10 percent is 6, and 5 percent is 3, so 15 percent is 9.
trap: finding 15% by subtracting 15.
Fix: say find 10 percent first, and they build it.
notes.help: Write the 10% step first, every time.
notes.prep: Build any percentage from 10% and 5%: the critical feature. SC2.

slides.title: What is 10% of 350?
slides.prompt: Point to A, B or C

options.misconception: subtracts 10 instead of finding a tenth

beats: SAY: Think about which benchmark this is.
ASK: What is 10 percent of 350?
10 sec. Cue: Voices off. Point... now. Hold your point.
EXPECT: pointing to A
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then cold call one student: What percentage is C?
Less -> say 10 percent is one tenth, and divide by 10. Re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: It's A, 35: one tenth of 350.
B took away 10, and C is 1 percent.
trap: pointing to B.
Fix: say 10 percent means one tenth, and they choose again.
notes.prep: First decision point. B: subtracting; C: 1% for 10%.

slides.title: Percentage of an amount
slides.ask: Find the percentage of the amount.
slides.followUp: cold call one board: Which benchmark did you start from?

items.say: 10 percent is 20, so 40 percent is 80, plus 5 percent, 10.

say: Write each answer on your board.
trap: subtracting the percentage from the amount.
Fix: say find 10 percent first, and they build it.
notes.help: Draw a bar and split it into tenths.
notes.prep: Guided practice: each benchmark, then a built percentage. SC1 and SC2.

beats: SAY: This one is just for you.
Start from your benchmark.
ASK: What is 35 percent of 60?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 21
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then Your turn.
Less -> find 10 percent together, 6, then build 30 and 5. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 10 percent is 6, 30 percent is 18,
and 5 percent is 3: 21. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 25, by subtracting.
Fix: say find 10 percent first, and they build it.
notes.prep: The hinge before independent work. Anyone writing 25 or 95 starts on the Supported Worksheet with the teacher.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Find percentages of amounts on your worksheet.

beats: POINT to the steps.
SAY: Read each question carefully, solve it carefully, then check your answers.
SAY: If you finish, the Extension is your early finisher option.
Let's read the steps together. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE and ask: Which benchmark did you start from?
TIME: 20 minutes. Stop everyone once at 10 minutes to share a strategy.
trap: subtracting the percentage.
Fix: say find 10 percent first, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: Extension: working backwards, comparing deals and a percentage increase.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: benchmarks only, a step frame and hints.
notes.prep: Independent practice: benchmarks, building from 10%, a mistake, and sport and shopping. The sheet is evidence for SC2 and SC3.

beats: SAY: Here's the last one. Work it out on your own board.
ASK: What is 45 percent of 120?
40 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 54
RECORD who subtracts or slips building from 10%.
Their names go to next week's catch-up group.
trap: writing 75.
Fix: none now. Record the name for tomorrow.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2 across the week: a built percentage of a new amount.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner how to find any percentage of an amount.

notes.answer: open - listen for find 10 percent first, then build
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can find a percentage of an amount?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit board.
A thumb up with 75 on the board matters most.
ASK: How can you find any percentage of an amount?
20 sec. Cue: Partner A first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: find 10 percent first, then build
notes.prep: Week close: read the self-assessment beside the exit evidence for next week's review.
